stem.en: Under the kudavolai system recorded at Uttaramerur, how did a person come to serve on a village committee?

text.en: A king's officer read out a list of the people he had chosen.
The largest landowner named the people he trusted.
An eligible candidate's name was written on a palm leaf, a child drew it from a pot, and those chosen were divided into committees.
The villagers raised their hands for each candidate in turn, and the highest count won.

explanation.en: The names of eligible candidates were written on palm leaves and placed in a large pot. At a public gathering a young child drew the leaves one by one. The elected members were then divided into specialised committees called variyams.

hints.en: Think of the leaves, the pot and the child.
The source describes a draw, with no count of raised hands.
